title: Every Imaging-screen capture loses its filter: FITS has no FILTER card, filename says "NoFilter", DB filter column is empty
what_happened: With the simulated filter wheel connected and reporting slot 2 = R, I took a 30 s light. The file was written as /tmp/Unknown_NoFilter_2026-08-01_0001.fits, its header contains no FILTER keyword at all, and captured_images.filter is the empty string. I then clicked the Ha chip (log: 'api_filterwheel_set_position called: device_id=sim_filterwheel_1, position=4', wheel moved, chip highlighted Ha) and took a second 5 s light - identical result: Unknown_NoFilter_..._0002.fits, no FILTER card, filter='' in the DB. All 11 frames captured in the session have filter=''. Root cause: the only construction site of FilterWheelSelector (imaging_bottom_banner.dart:552-556) omits the `onFilterSelected` callback, and grep shows ZERO callers anywhere pass it, so nothing ever writes the filter name into exposureSettingsProvider. persistence.dart:57 then reads `filter: exposureSettings.filter`, which is always null.
expected: FILTER = 'Ha' in the FITS header, 'Ha' in the filename, and 'Ha' in captured_images.filter - the wheel is connected and the app already knows and displays the active filter name on the same screen.
repro: 1. Onboard with the Sim backend (camera + filter wheel with L R G B Ha OIII SII). 2. Equipment -> Connect All. 3. Imaging -> Capture tab, exposure 30 -> Snapshot. 4. Click the Ha chip in the bottom banner, Snapshot again. 5. `python3` dump of the FITS header and `sqlite3 skotiq.db 'select file_name,filter from captured_images'`.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-32-ha.png (Ha chip active), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-filters.png (R highlighted before the change), header dump: EXPTIME=5.0, DATE-OBS, IMAGETYP='Light', GAIN=100 ... no FILTER card; sqlite: `2|Unknown_NoFilter_2026-08-01_0002.fits||5.0`
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/imaging/widgets/imaging_bottom_banner.dart:552 (FilterWheelSelector built with no onFilterSelected); packages/skotiq_app/lib/widgets/filter_wheel_selector.dart:32,88-91 (callback declared, never supplied); packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/imaging_service/persistence.dart:57
proposed_fix: Pass onFilterSelected from the banner and have it set exposureSettingsProvider.filter (and filterPosition). Better: make persistence.dart read the live filterWheelStateProvider name as the source of truth instead of a UI-mirrored copy, so no future call site can drop it.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced independently in my own instance (display :87, profile imaging-guiding-verify). The sim filter wheel was connected with names [L,R,G,B,Ha,OIII,SII] and the log shows `api_filterwheel_set_position called: device_id=sim_filterwheel_1, position=4` at 15:22:48; the 5 s light taken at 15:23:08 was written as /tmp/ns-verify-caps/Unknown_NoFilter_2026-08-01_0002.fits with NO FILTER card (verified by dumping the 80-char header cards), and `sqlite3 skotiq.db 'select file_name,filter from captured_images'` returns filter='' for all 22 frames in the profile. Code confirms: imaging_bottom_banner.dart:552 is the only construction of FilterWheelSelector and it omits onFilterSelected (declared filter_wheel_selector.dart:24/32, fired at :88-91); camera_panel.dart and capture_panel.dart contain no filter control at all, so the banner strip is the Imaging screen's only filter UI; persistence.dart:55 reads `filter: exposureSettings.filter`. Two corrections. (1) 'grep shows ZERO callers anywhere pass it / nothing ever writes the filter name into exposureSettingsProvider' is overstated: dashboard/widgets/capture_settings_card.dart:411,439 and widgets/capture_settings_panel.dart:420,439 both do `copyWith(filter: ...)` after the wheel settles — the Dashboard capture card tags frames correctly (capture_settings_panel.dart has no call sites, it is dead code). (2) The sequencer path is unaffected: FitsWriteHeaderRich::from_frame_context (api/imaging.rs:3384) sets filter from ctx.filter_name and save_fits_file_rich writes FILTER + FILTPOS at :3692-3696. So this is a manual-Imaging-screen data-integrity bug, not an every-frame one — P1, not P0.

title: Framing "Add to Sequence -> Add target" silently adds nothing: the Sequencer still shows 0 targets
what_happened: On the Framing screen with M92 resolved (RA 17h17m07s, Dec +43 08' 12", 'Target Resolved' green), I clicked Utilities -> Add to Sequence. A dialog opened: 'Insert "M92" as a new target group. You add the imaging instructions under it in the Sequencer.' with 'New empty sequence' pre-selected. I clicked 'Add target'. The dialog closed with no toast, no error and no navigation. Navigating to Sequencer shows 'New Sequence - 0 targets - 1 node - Sequence 0 steps - Drop instructions here'. The database confirms it: sequences=0, sequence_nodes=0, sequence_versions=0.
expected: A Target node named M92 with its RA/Dec appears in the sequence tree (header should read '1 target'), or the flow reports why it could not be created.
repro: 1. Plan Tonight -> Recommendation -> M92 card -> Send to Framing. 2. Scroll the Framing sidebar to Utilities. 3. Add to Sequence -> keep 'New empty sequence' -> Add target. 4. Nav -> Sequencer. 5. `sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/imaging-guiding/data/skotiq.db 'select count(*) from sequences; select count(*) from sequence_nodes;'`
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-107-addseq2.png (dialog with M92 named), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-109-sequencer.png ('0 targets', 'Sequence 0 steps'), sqlite output: sequences=0, sequence_nodes=0, sequence_versions=0
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/framing/widgets/add_target_to_sequence_flow.dart (dialog confirms but the resulting node never reaches the sequencer provider or the DB)
proposed_fix: Await and check the insert result, then either navigate to /sequencer with the new target selected or surface the failure. A confirm dialog that returns silently on both success and failure is exactly how this shipped undetected.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced end-to-end. Plan Tonight -> M92 -> Send to Framing -> Utilities -> Add to Sequence opened the dialog 'Insert "M92" as a new target group...' with 'New empty sequence' selected; I clicked 'Add target' (click landed dead-centre of the button, root 1120,707 vs button bounds root x1079-1166 y695-721). The dialog closed with no toast and no navigation; `select count(*) from sequences` / `sequence_nodes` stayed 0/0; navigating to Sequencer shows 'New Sequence | 0 targets | 1 node | Sequence 0 steps | Drop instructions here'. The sequence name is decisive: add_target_to_sequence_flow.dart:225 would have called createSequence(name: 'M92'), so the header would read 'M92', not 'New Sequence' — the create/addTargetHeader path demonstrably did not take effect. framing_screen.dart:474 shows a snackbar only `if (added)`, and none appeared. Severity corrected to P1: it is a broken primary workflow with a silent failure, but nothing is lost or corrupted and the user can build the target by hand in the Sequencer.

title: Loop (live view) writes every frame to disk as a full-size FITS and registers it in the database - ~7.5 MB/s
what_happened: I pressed Loop with a 5 s exposure and let it run ~25 s, then pressed Stop. In that window the app wrote 8 new 23,394,240-byte FITS files into the capture folder (plus thumbnails) and inserted 8 rows into captured_images. There is no 'save frames' toggle anywhere in the Loop UI. Extrapolated: framing/focusing with Loop for one hour at 5 s subs writes ~27 GB of junk lights named Unknown_NoFilter_*, all of which land in the user's light-frame folder and in the session integration total.
expected: Loop is a live-view/framing mode - NINA, SGP and SharpCap all discard live-view frames unless you explicitly ask to save. At minimum there should be a visible 'Save loop frames' switch, defaulted off.
repro: 1. Imaging, set Dur 5 s. 2. `ls /tmp/*.fits | wc -l` (baseline 3). 3. Press Loop, wait 25 s, press Stop. 4. `ls /tmp/*.fits | wc -l` -> 11; `du -ch /tmp/*.fits` -> 246 MB; `select count(*) from captured_images` -> 11.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-58-loop.png (Exposing 24%, loop running), `ls -lat /tmp/*.fits` showing 0001_001, 0002_001, 0003_001, 0004..0008 all timestamped 10:24-10:25, `du -ch /tmp/*.fits` = 246M total, session panel 'Captured 11 frames / Integration 1m 20s'
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/imaging/imaging_screen/imaging_screen_actions.dart (loop path calls the same save-and-persist pipeline as Snapshot)
proposed_fix: Route loop frames through the preview path only (no _saveFitsFile / _saveToDatabase), and add an explicit opt-in toggle next to the Loop button if keeping frames is wanted. Also note the collision-avoidance naming produced 0001_001/0002_001/0003_001 before jumping to 0004 - the sequence counter is not monotonic across app state.
verdict_reasoning: Confirmed in code and in my profile's data. imaging_screen_actions.dart:216 calls imagingService.startLoopCapture, which (imaging_service.dart:812-819) calls the same captureImage() used by Snapshot, and captureImage unconditionally runs _saveFitsFile (imaging_service.dart:455) and _saveToDatabase (:483). The evidence is in the scratch profile: two back-to-back loop bursts are visible as consecutive full-size writes — rows 3-8 at 15:24:04/10/16/22/28/34/40 (5 s subs, ~6 s cadence) and rows 12-21 at 15:39:16 through 15:39:56 (3 s subs, ~4 s cadence) — each file 23,394,240 bytes with a .thumb.jpg beside it, all registered in captured_images and all named Unknown_NoFilter_*. No 'save loop frames' control exists anywhere in the capture banner (Snapshot | Loop | Dur | Gain | filter chips | Stretch). The side observation about 0001_001/0002_001 naming is the _ensureUniqueFilePath collision suffix (file_paths.dart:66-80), which is by design, not a broken counter. P1 is right.

title: Framing "GoTo & Frame - Ready" with a PARKED mount and a target 5.7 deg below the horizon; Slew to Target is a silent no-op
what_happened: Framing wizard step 4 'GoTo & Frame' displayed a green 'Ready' badge and a filled primary 'Slew to Target' button. At that moment the sidebar's own Coordinates card said 'Alt -5.7 deg / Target below horizon' and the mount was Parked (Imaging -> Mount tab: 'Mount Status STOPPED, RA 00h 00m 0.0s, Dec +00 00' 0.0", Status Parked'). I clicked Slew to Target three times, and once through the split-button menu item 'Slew'. Nothing happened: no dialog, no toast, no error banner, zero new lines in app.log, and the mount was still Parked at RA 00h00m/Dec +00 afterwards.
expected: Either the step reports 'Not ready - mount is parked' and disables the button, or clicking it says 'Mount is parked - unpark first' / 'Target is 5.7 deg below the horizon - slew anyway?'. A green Ready plus a primary button that does nothing is the worst of both.
repro: 1. Connect sim mount (it comes up Parked). 2. Plan Tonight -> M92 -> Send to Framing. 3. Scroll the sidebar to step 4. 4. Click 'Slew to Target'. 5. `tail` app.log (no new lines) and check Imaging -> Mount tab (still Parked, RA 00h00m).
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/imaging-guiding-91-slew2.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-slew3.png ('GoTo & Frame  Ready' + enabled Slew to Target), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-framing-scroll3.png ('Alt -5.7 / Target below horizon'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/crop-mountstate.png (Status Parked, RA 00h 00m 0.0s after 3 slew attempts), zero new app.log lines across all attempts
proposed_fix: Derive step-4 readiness from mountState.isParked && !isTracking && target altitude, and make the slew action surface its own failure via a snackbar. Also log the refusal - a completely silent log is why this looks like a dead button rather than a safety interlock.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with M92 in my instance. Framing sidebar step 4 shows a green 'Ready' pill and a filled primary 'Slew to Target'; the Coordinates card on the same sidebar reads 'Alt -1.7 / Az 25.2 / Target below horizon'; and Imaging -> Mount reads 'Mount Status STOPPED, RA 00h 00m 0.0s, Dec +00 00' 0.0", Status Parked'. I clicked the primary button twice and then opened its split menu (the chevron does open a Slew / Slew & Center popup) and selected 'Slew': no dialog, no snackbar within 2-3 s, zero new lines in app.log (1162 before and after; the entire 1162-line log contains no line matching 'lew'), and the mount was still Parked at RA 00h00m afterwards. Readiness confirmed in source: framing_actions_panel.dart:147 `final canSlew = hasTarget && isMountConnected;` — park state, tracking and altitude are not consulted, and :280 renders that as 'Ready'. Note that mount_command_service.slewTo (:179-206) always returns a CommandActionResult and SlewDropdownButton._handleSlew always calls showCommandActionResult, so the total silence means the command never reached the service — either way the user is told nothing. P1 stands.
